profile.claim: No production, drop-in or support claim. A row is evidence for the exact tested head only.

deployment.topology: one standalone process, one owner-local data path, no replication or cluster
deployment.persistence: private append-only journal only (appendfsync always|everysec|no); RDB, online backup and PITR excluded

declared_divergences.reason: The bounded PFDEBUG surface accepts a variable-argument form; both pinned references declare a fixed arity of 3. PFDEBUG payload interchange remains excluded (C10).
Private keyspace digest that follows the Redis 8.10.2 name; Valkey 9.1.2 does not ship it. It is not a drop-in requirement.
Conditional delete shipped after both pinned reference revisions. Published as a candidate extension, not a compatibility row.
Redis 8.10.2 conditional delete variant; Valkey 9.1.2 does not ship it. The candidate follows the Redis name.
Redis 8.10.2 set cardinality command; Valkey 9.1.2 does not ship it.
Redis 8.10.2 set cardinality command; Valkey 9.1.2 does not ship it.

declared_noops.reason: Replication is excluded (A1). The legacy no-replica form returns +OK while changing no topology; REPLICAOF and FAILOVER return explicit unsupported errors. Declared here so clients are not silently misled.

clients.evidence: Pinned redis-cli RESP2/RESP3 rows in this profile matrix plus the pinned Tcl matrix.
Official workload generator used by the protected performance gates; not a behavioral client row.
Pinned C7 language-client matrix: 14 declared cases (handshake, AUTH/ACL, RESP2/3, pipeline, transaction, pub/sub, TLS, reconnect, error paths).
Pinned C7 language-client matrix: the same 14 declared cases with node-redis 6.4.0.
Pinned C7 language-client matrix: the same 14 declared cases with go-redis v9.14.0.
Any client whose discovery or error handling depends on unlisted commands or RESP3 attributes is unsupported.

exclusions.reason: No Lua runtime under the dependency policy; every execution entry point must fail closed instead of silently succeeding.
Flushing an empty script/function registry is the only accepted administrative form; it is a documented no-op, not execution support.
Loadable modules are excluded; MODULE LOAD must fail closed. The native controls also refuse module loading because the module command is disabled in the harness configuration.
Database 0 is the only keyspace; SELECT, SWAPDB and MOVE to another database must be rejected without mutating data.
COPY DB n with n != 0 must be rejected without creating the destination key.
RDB snapshots are excluded; the private append-only journal is the only persistence mechanism.
No interoperable DUMP/RESTORE/MIGRATE payload exists; these must fail closed rather than emit or accept a private blob.
Replication and failover are excluded; topology commands must fail closed. The legacy SLAVEOF NO ONE no-op is declared in commands.declared_noops.
Idle time and LFU frequency are not tracked; the profile excludes them instead of fabricating values.
LATENCY GRAPH is excluded; LATENCY HISTORY is the supported diagnostic.
Startup configuration is read-only; there is no writable redis.conf language.

declared_row_divergences.reason: XPENDING reports a per-consumer pending count as an integer and an empty pending summary as an empty array; both pinned references use a bulk string and a null array. Frozen so any change is reviewed rather than silently accepted.
For a consumer group that has not read, XINFO GROUPS reports entries-read as 0; both pinned references report a null bulk. Frozen so the exact public-field difference stays visible.
An unknown command returns the bounded 'ERR unknown command' text without echoing client-supplied bytes; Redis 8.10.2 echoes the command name. Frozen verbatim.
An unknown command returns the bounded 'ERR unknown command' text without echoing client-supplied bytes; Valkey 9.1.2 echoes the command name and leading arguments. Frozen verbatim.
